description: Single storey rear extension; external alterations; conversion of dwellinghouse into three self contained flats (1 x  1 bed; 1 x 2 beds and 1 x 3 beds); hard surfacing to front garden to provide three parking spaces; bin / cycle storage (part demolition of rear extension)
decision_conditions: <p>Proposed Flat 2, indicated on the first and second floors of the development by reason of its designation as a 2-bedroom, 3-person dwelling, would fail to provide the minimum four bed spaces required for a 2-bedroom unit under Policy HO1(A2) of the Local Plan. The proposal would therefore fail to provide suitably sized and flexible residential accommodation capable of meeting the changing needs of occupants and would undermine the objectives of preventing overcrowding and securing high-quality housing. The development is therefore contrary to Policy HO1(2) of the Local Plan (2021 - 2041) and is unacceptable in principle.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>

<p>The proposed development fails to demonstrate satisfactory vertical stacking of habitable rooms, resulting in an unacceptable relationship between internal uses across floors. In particular, habitable rooms would be positioned above and/or below non-habitable spaces, increasing the potential for noise and disturbance between units and resulting in a poor standard of residential accommodation for future occupiers. As such, the proposal would fail to provide a high-quality living environment and would be contrary to Policy D6 of the London Plan (2021), Policy GR1 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041), the Residential Design Guide SPD (2010) and the Mayor's Housing SPG (2023).&nbsp;</p>

<p>The proposed development fails to provide satisfactory and usable amenity space for future occupiers. The proposed communal rear garden would not be directly accessible from any of the proposed flats and would instead require residents to exit the building, access a public alleyway, and re-enter the rear garden. This fragmented and inconvenient arrangement would significantly undermine the functionality, accessibility and likely use of the amenity space, resulting in a poor standard of residential accommodation contrary to Policy D3, subsection D(7) and Policy D6, subsection (D) of The London Plan (2021), Policy GR1 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041), the Residential Design Guide SPD (2010) and the Mayor's Housing SPG (2023).&nbsp;</p>

<p>The proposed development fails to provide safe, convenient and suitably integrated cycle and refuse storage facilities. Access to the proposed stores would be via a shared public right of way used by both pedestrians and vehicles, requiring the movement of cycles and refuse containers across this route. This arrangement would give rise to conflict between users, prejudice pedestrian safety, and result in an inconvenient and impractical means of access for future occupiers. Consequently, the proposal would fail to deliver appropriate servicing and cycle parking provision and would result in a poor standard of residential accommodation, contrary to the objectives of the Policies D4, T5 and SI 8 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies GR1, M2, M3 and CE1 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021 – 2041) and Harrow’s Code of Practice for Storage and Collection of Refuse and Materials for Recycling in Domestic Properties (2023) which seek to ensure safe, functional and well-designed development.&nbsp;</p>

<p>The proposed development represents an over-intensive and contrived form of development which would result in a poor design impacting the character of the area and poor standard of residential accommodation for future occupiers. The scheme fails to provide a satisfactory landscaping strategy, resulting in limited opportunities for soft landscaping and an unsatisfactory living environment. As such, the proposal would be contrary to Policies D6 and G5 of the London Plan (2021), Policies GR1 and GI4 of the Harrow Local Plan (2021-2041), the Residential Design Guide SPD (2010) and the Mayor's Housing SPG (2023) which seek to secure high-quality residential accommodation and well-designed development that responds appropriately to its site and surroundings&nbsp;</p>
